paragraphs.source_en: If things were really to turn out “just as one wished” for me, that would be rather troublesome. As for what death is like, I have not yet experienced it, so I cannot say whether I like it or dislike it. But the other day something happened: because it was terribly cold, I crawled into the fire-extinguishing jar to warm myself, and the cook, Osan, not knowing I was inside, put the lid on from above. Even now, when I remember the agony of being smothered then, it frightens me. According to Miss White Cat, if that suffocation had lasted a little longer, I would have died. I have, of course, no objection to dying in Miss Mike’s place. However, if one cannot die without undergoing that agony, then I do not wish to die for anyone.

paragraphs.source_en: Lately I have lost the courage to go out; for some reason the world feels utterly wearisome to me, and I have become a lazy cat no less indolent than my master. paragraphs.source_zh: 最近，我已失去了外出的勇气，不知为什么，我感到人世毫无意义，变成个不比主人差的懒猫了。别人说主人整天蜷伏在书斋里是因为失恋。现在想来，这个说法不无道理。

paragraphs.source_en: I have not yet caught a single mouse, and for a time the cook Osan even proposed expelling me. But because my master knows well that I am no ordinary cat, I am still allowed to live idly in this house. On this point, while I am grateful for my master’s kindness, I also cannot help admiring his keen eye for recognizing talent. That Osan, unable to recognize my extraordinary qualities, mistreats me from time to time does not especially anger me. Before long Hidari Jingoro will appear and carve my portrait on the pillar of a tower gate, and Japan’s Steinlen will gladly paint my likeness on canvas; then those blind fellows will be ashamed of their own lack of discernment.
